lessons.title: PHP execution and request boundaries
lessons.intro:
PHP 8.2+; snippets are inside a PHP block. PHP runs in different server APIs, including CLI and web servers. A web request receives its own execution context; ordinary local variables do not persist across later requests. CLI arguments arrive through argv, while query and form values use superglobals. php -l checks syntax without executing the script. Keep declarations before use, and distinguish the language interpreter from the server that routes HTTP requests. These examples assume PHP 8.2 or later.

Read each snippet, identify its effect, then complete a fragment. Examples are independent unless stated otherwise. Snippets may omit surrounding entry points and standard imports; displayed code is never executed by the tutor.

lessons.title: PDO parameters and transactional boundaries
lessons.intro:
PHP 8.2+; snippets are inside a PHP block. PDO is PHP's standard database interface, provided by an extension with a driver for the selected database. These questions assume PDO_SQLite is available. Prepare statements with placeholders and bind data through execute rather than concatenating SQL. Parameters represent values, not table names or SQL keywords. Transactions group related writes; catch failures and roll back at the application boundary. SQLite is used for small fixtures, not as a claim that all database dialects behave identically.
